_comment.this file: How the feature registry is laid out and checked — read by scripts/process/registry_config.py for the registry gate (feature-registry module), check_product_frame, check_issues and check_plan_structure. The defaults are the template's registry (docs/process/modules/feature-registry.md). PROJECT CHOICES go into docs/process/feature-registry.local.json, laid over this file: mappings merge key by key, everything else (lists included) replaces whole. Both files are gate configuration: a change owes a refute. An unknown key fails the registry gate; `_comment` is allowed at any level.
_comment.layout: "flat": one <id>.json per story directly in `root`. "capabilities": one directory per capability holding a head `_capability.json` (schema_version 1, capability = directory name, prefix when id_pattern uses {prefix}; further head fields are the project's) and one <id>.json per story. JSON directly in `root` is then an error, except *.example.json.
_comment.root: The registry directory, relative to the repository root.
_comment.id_pattern: A story id, as a regular expression. In the capabilities layout {prefix} is the capability's `prefix` from its head, e.g. "^{prefix}-US-\\d{3}$". Prose refers to a story in the loose form (any digit width, between word boundaries).
_comment.require_registry: false: an absent or empty registry is a note. true: an absent root, no capability or an empty capability fails.
_comment.story_text_fields: Story fields that must be non-empty strings.
_comment.story_surfaces: "none": stories carry no `surfaces`. "optional" / "required": a story's `surfaces` is a non-empty subset of `surfaces` (required: it must be there).
_comment.surfaces: The project's declared surfaces (platforms). Empty: an item has one implicit surface.
_comment.shared_proof_layers: Layers whose tests prove an item for every surface of it, when the item says `owned_by` that layer (e.g. ["backend"]).
_comment.story_tests: "tests": a non-empty list of test refs on the story, at least one of them an existing test. "test_mapping": a non-empty object from surface or shared proof layer to a non-empty list of test refs.
_comment.issues: The story's issue field. `field`: "issue" (one ref) or "issues" (a list, which may be empty). `required`: the field must be there. `required_for`: a story status (from story_status.values) that needs at least one ref. The ref format is check_review.parse_issue_ref's (#N, owner/repo#N, a GitHub issue URL).
_comment.story_status: null: `status` stays retired (issues own what is in flight). An object {"values": [...], "deferred": "deferred", "deferred_allows_empty_tests": true}: `status` is required and one of `values`; a `deferred` story may leave a test_mapping list empty when allowed.
_comment.test_ref_roots: Prefixes every test ref must start with (e.g. ["backend/", "ios/"]). Empty: any path in the repository.
_comment.planned_refs: true: a test ref may be a placeholder `planned:#<issue>:<description>`. A placeholder is never proof.
_comment.node_check: How a dead `path::node` selector counts: "note" or "hard". Each `::` segment is checked — in a .py file against the names it defines (AST), in any other file as a substring. An unparsable .py file counts the same way.
_comment.retired_fields: Story fields that fail as retired. A project list replaces this one whole. With story_status set, `status` is no longer retired.
_comment.extra_fields: Further story fields the project knows (e.g. ["notes"]); other unknown fields are a note.
_comment.strict_item_tests: true: an acceptance item without an existing test fails. false: such items are counted in one note per capability (or inventory).
